newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong passenger describes China air crash.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong passenger describes China air crash.

text.p: A Hong Kong man who survived China's worst aviation disaster in three years told reporters from his hospital bed on Friday the pilot ordered passengers to the centre of the plane just seconds before it crashed.
At least 35 people were killed in the Boeing 737-300 crash, Chinese officials said.
The victim, who gave his name as Fung, told Hong Kong reporters he was in a window seat observing torrential rain when the order came.
The pilot ordered all passengers to sit in the centre of the aircraft while he attempted to land.
It was all over in a split second, said Fung, who sustained head injuries when the impact flung him against the seat in front.

China Southern Airlines flight CZ3456 from the southwestern city of Chongqing slammed into the tarmac during a thunderstorm at an airport in Shenzhen, a prosperous city on the Chinese border with Hong Kong, local officials said.
The aircraft carrying 65 passengers and crew broke up and burned when it smashed into the ground at the new Huangtian airport.
The flight was diverted from Shenzhen's international airport to Huangtian because of the heavy rain.
